wi_heavenly_boulders.blurb: Heavenly Boulders is a small cluster of boulders on Devil's Lake's West Bluff, up the slope from the Dumpster Boulder and reached from the Tumbled Rocks trail by following the southern edge of the Pete's Pebble talus field uphill for a couple hundred yards. Twelve problems here run from V0 up to V7, with the bulk in the V3 to V5 range, so it suits climbers who already have some bouldering mileage. The boulders sit in the West Bluff Central section, a spread-out talus zone below the West Rampart, and a hard V7 line draws visiting boulderers. Expect a short but steep haul from the trail.

wi_09_prayer_wall.blurb: Prayer Wall is a trad and top-rope wall in the east-bluff talus at Devil's Lake State Park in the Baraboo Range. The main face looks southeast and is split by two well-defined cracks. Around a dozen routes here range from easy 5.4 terrain through the 5.6 and 5.7 range to a few 5.10 lines, and most are short, roughly 30 to 40 feet. Footholds can be sparse on the classic Devil's Lake edges, so it rewards solid crack and face technique. It is a good stop for moderate trad leaders and for anyone setting up top-ropes on the quieter side of the east bluff.

wi_slab_area.blurb: Slab Area is a small, tucked-away bouldering zone inside Westby Bouldering, in Davidson Park near Westby, roughly 20 miles from La Crosse. The sandstone here is slopey, and the section is known for a tall slab with excellent movement. Of the dozen problems, most fall between V1 and V2 or around V5, with one considerably harder line. This part of the rock is slow to dry after rain, sometimes needing an extra day, and fall is the best season for good friction. Parking on the nearby street gives a short approach, and the zone is visible from the road.

wi_prow_aka_tunder_tighs_the.blurb: The Prow is a boulder in the Massive Vertigo Area on Devil's Lake's West Bluff North, a relatively underdeveloped part of the lake that is mostly talus fields scattered with trees. Twelve problems share the block, spanning moderate V2 up to V10, though the bulk are hard, mostly between V6 and V8. The classic line is a steep V7, and neighbouring problems include a V10 and a V4+ plus a V5. This is a spot for strong boulderers who want powerful moves rather than a beginner circuit.

nh_the_whip.blurb: The Whip is a boulder at Round Pond in Pawtuckaway State Park, New Hampshire, standing just left of Fancy Boulders and inside the loop of the path. Twelve boulder problems climb here, ranging from V1 to V13, though most sit in the V3 to V4 band, with a few much harder outliers. The namesake line is a V2 layback crack, a popular classic. Round Pond is a small, compact bouldering zone, and fall is the favourite season for it.

nh_old_gold.blurb: Old Gold is a large boulder at Round Pond in Pawtuckaway State Park, New Hampshire, sitting just outside the loop path, left of The Whip. It holds twelve problems from V0 to V4+, mostly in the V3 to V4 range, with a few easier lines. That makes it a friendly stop for intermediate boulderers working through the Round Pond circuit, which is a small compact area best in the fall.
